memoryText: Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Revelation 5:12 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Count the attributes in this one verse: power, wealth, wisdom, might, honor, glory, blessing. Seven, the number of completeness. Everything good that anyone could give to anyone is given to the Lamb. And he is worthy, not because of what he has but because of what he did: he was slain.

Think about who the Lamb is. He is the Son of God, and he took on flesh, bore the sins of the world, and was killed. Heaven’s greatest worship is for the one who was slaughtered. This reveals what God values. Not conquest by force, but love poured out. Worth is measured at the cross.

This verse can be sung in the car, whispered in a hospital, or shouted at a graveside. When your worth is questioned, or when you feel powerless, remember that the worthy one died for you. Say it aloud, and add your voice to the angels’ choir.
weekInReview: This week you read the letters to the churches and the opening of the seals. Revelation 3 gave Jesus’ words to Sardis (alive in name only), Philadelphia (faithful with little power, given an open door), and Laodicea (lukewarm and self-satisfied, with Christ knocking at the door). Three psalms reflected on the way of the blessed (Psalm 1), the glory of creation and the word (Psalm 19), and the voice of the LORD in the storm (Psalm 29). Revelation 4 and 5 brought us into the throne room, with the worship of the Creator and the Lion who is a Lamb, worthy to open the scroll because he was slain and ransomed people from every nation. Revelation 6 showed the Lamb opening six seals: conquest, war, famine, death, the cry of the martyrs, and the wrath of the Lamb, ending with the question, “who can stand?”
reflectionQuestions: Jesus tells Laodicea, “Behold, I stand at the door and knock.” Is there an area where you have been keeping him outside? What would it look like to open the door today?
John expected a Lion and saw a Lamb. How does the way Jesus won, through sacrifice, change the way you think about strength, success, and winning?
The martyrs cry, “How long?” and are told to rest a little longer. What are you waiting on God for? How can you trust that he hears?
prayerPrompts: Worship the Lamb who was slain.
Thank him that he holds the scroll of history.
